title: Fish a bottle cap out from under a toaster oven with a wooden spoon's handle, without shoving the oven
instruction: A bottle cap has rolled under the toaster oven. Get it out with the wooden spoon without moving the oven, then put the spoon down and move your hands away.
context: Something rolling under a countertop appliance is an everyday kitchen mishap, and the usual fix is the same everywhere: slide a spoon handle or a ruler under, get it behind the object and draw it out. The toaster oven stands only 22 mm off the counter on four rubber feet set well in from its sides, so the cap cannot be seen from above, no finger fits under, and a straight push only sends it deeper. The handle has to go in between the feet, past the cap, and be drawn back so the cap comes with it, without knocking the feet and shoving the 6 kg oven.
setup: Bench top is z = 0.7475 m; x points away from the arm bases (0.6 m apart at the bench's near edge), y to their left. All poses fixed. Toaster oven: a 6 kg countertop oven, 300 mm deep x 440 mm wide x 210 mm high body, front face at x 0.25, centred on y 0, standing 22 mm off the bench on four 24 mm rubber feet 50 mm in from the front and back and 100 mm in from the sides. Cap: a 30 mm x 12 mm polyethylene soda-bottle cap, 4 g, lying open side down under the oven at x 0.42, y -0.19 (30 mm in from the right side, 170 mm in from the front). Spoon: a 330 mm beech wooden spoon (260 x 14 x 9 mm handle, 70 x 50 mm bowl), 45 g, lying on the bench to the right of the oven along y, bowl toward the arms' right, handle tip at x 0.30, y -0.27. Dimensions, masses and friction are in parameters.py and README.md.
scoring: Measured with a ruler from the cap to the nearest edge of the oven's footprint as it stood at the start (tape marks at its feet), and watched on video for what moves the cap. 0.25: the cap's centre within 10 mm of the footprint's edge. 0.5: its centre out past the edge. 0.75: the whole cap out. 1.0: the cap at least 20 mm clear of the footprint, the spoon laid down on the bench and let go of, and both hands out from under and around the oven, held for 1 s. 0 if at any time the oven moves more than 5 mm or turns more than 2 degrees from its marks, if the cap is moved more than 10 mm by anything but the spoon, or if the cap is knocked off the bench.
reset_notes: Put the oven back on its tape marks, lay the cap open side down at its mark under the oven (reach it in from behind or lift the oven), and lay the spoon at its outline.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz, real gripper contact. The oven (6 kg on four rubber feet, mu 1.0), cap (PE, mu 0.35) and spoon (beech, mu 0.40) are free rigid bodies moved by contact only: no rules, joints or attachments. Approximations: the spoon is two rigid boxes (a 14 x 9 mm handle and a flat 50 x 70 mm bowl) rather than its rounded shape, with no flex; the oven is a box with its door and handle as visual detail.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 993 steps (49.65 simulated seconds); termination: task_budget_limit. Scripted/teleoperated demo: 1 after 317 steps.
